title: Dancing with the SARs — Planet & Amazon Surface Change Atlas (2020–2026)

manaus.name: Manaus — Rio Negro / Solimões Confluence
manaus.why: Anchor gauge for the record June 2021 flood (30.02 m), 2023 drought (12.70 m), 2024 historic low (12.11 m), and real 2026 NISAR L-band Track 140 acquisitions capturing seasonal flood vs. dry transition over flooded igapó forest.

porto_velho.name: Porto Velho — Middle Madeira River Floodplain
porto_velho.why: Southern Amazon tributary where the seasonal flood wave peaks in Mar–Apr—two months before Manaus—and where Oct dry-season lows expose extensive rocky/sandy shoals.

tefe.name: Lake Tefé & Mamirauá Várzea (Middle Solimões)
tefe.why: Epicentre of the Sep–Nov 2023 severe drought crisis (lake contraction and 39.1 °C water) next to Mamirauá várzea flooded forest.

apui_labrea.name: Apuí–Lábrea Deforestation & Fire Frontier (BR-230)
apui_labrea.why: Active human-driven frontier showing Jun–Oct geometric forest clearing followed by Aug–Oct slash burning through thick smoke plumes using all-weather C- and L-band SAR.

global_aus_nsw.name: Australia Black Summer Burn Scars
global_aus_nsw.why: Sentinel-1 C-band cross-polarized VH backscatter penetrates pyrocumulonimbus smoke clouds over Clyde Mountain & Batemans Bay (NSW), revealing structural branch/canopy incineration immediately after Jan 2020.

global_pak_indus.name: Pakistan Indus Inland Sea Flood
global_pak_indus.why: Extreme 2022 monsoon created a ~100 km wide inland sea around Lake Manchar & Dadu in Sindh. Smooth mirror-like floodwaters reflect C-band radar away from Sentinel-1, turning inundated plains jet-black (< -15 dB).

global_tur_kahramanmaras.name: Türkiye–Syria Fault Slip & Urban Damage
global_tur_kahramanmaras.why: Synthetic Aperture Radar measures centimeter-to-meter crustal deformation across the East Anatolian Fault near Pazarcik and maps structural urban collapse via Sentinel-1 corner-reflector phase & amplitude decorrelation.

global_can_quebec.name: Canada Boreal Permafrost & Taiga Megafires
global_can_quebec.why: During Canada's historic 2023 wildfire season (>15M ha burned nationally), continental smoke cloaked North America for weeks while Sentinel-1 C-band VH radar continuously mapped expanding James Bay & Quebec burn scars.

global_ant_weddell.name: Antarctic Winter Sea-Ice Record Deficit
global_ant_weddell.why: In September 2023—supposed to be peak Austral winter freeze—Antarctic sea ice fell >1.6 million km² below its 1981–2010 maximum. Active SAR and passive microwave AMSR2 pierce polar night and Southern Ocean storms.

phenomena.name: Rainy season
phenomena.summary: Peak convective rainfall across the Amazon Basin (Dec–May, wettest Feb–Apr). Cloud-penetrating microwave radar monitors soil/canopy wetting and the multi-month floodplain recharge even when dense ITCZ clouds blind optical satellites.

sar_physics.roughness_mechanism: Dense Amazon terra firme crowns produce diffuse volume scattering across C- and L-band all year round, while smooth rising water surfaces begin turning dark via specular reflection.
sar_physics.dielectric_mechanism: Liquid water has a very high dielectric constant (~80 vs ~3–5 for dry vegetation/soil). Heavy wet-season rain raises leaf and soil moisture, boosting upper-canopy reflectivity (+0.6 to +1.2 dB in Sentinel-1 C-band VV) and triggering early inundated-forest returns.
sar_physics.polarization_note: VV tracks top-crown dielectric moisture + vertical stem scattering; VH preserves cross-polarized volume structure to separate rain-wet forest from open water.
sar_physics.frequency_comparison: C-band (5.6 cm) reacts strongly to leaf/twig surface wetness in the upper crown, whereas L-band (24 cm) passes cleanly through rain cells and upper leaves to inspect trunks.

drivers.natural_driver: Southward migration of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) and Amazon moisture convergence.
drivers.human_driver: Road washouts and wetland recharge pause heavy mechanized forest clearing during Dec–May.

phenomena.name: Seasonal flood
phenomena.typical_timing: Peak ~Mar - Jun (Madeira at Porto Velho: ~Mar - Apr)
phenomena.summary: Annual 10–12 meter Amazon flood-pulse wave. Southern tributaries like the Madeira River at Porto Velho crest early (~Mar–Apr), whereas the Rio Negro/Solimões mainstem at Manaus peaks later (~May–Jun).

sar_physics.roughness_mechanism: Two opposite roughness signatures appear side-by-side: calm open rivers become radar mirrors (specular reflection away from satellite, very dark), while flooded forest trunks standing in water form 90° corner reflectors.
sar_physics.dielectric_mechanism: High dielectric floodwater beneath várzea/igapó trees reflects incident microwaves forward onto vertical trunks and back to the sensor—producing intense trunk–water double-bounce (+3.5 to +5.5 dB enhancement).
sar_physics.polarization_note: HH (horizontal co-pol) maximizes double-bounce off horizontal water + vertical trunks; OPERA DSWx-S1 fuses C-band backscatter to classify Open Water vs. Inundated Vegetation.
sar_physics.frequency_comparison: Sentinel-1 C-band (5.6 cm) maps open channels and sparse inundated shrubs; NISAR L-band (24 cm) penetrates closed 30 m forest canopies to reveal hidden flooded forests beneath.

drivers.natural_driver: Asynchronous timing of southern Andes/Madeira rains (peaking Mar–Apr) vs. northern Rio Negro crest (May–Jun).
drivers.human_driver: Riverine várzea agriculture, floating stilt communities, and hydropower dams (Santo Antônio / Jirau near Porto Velho).

phenomena.name: Dry season
phenomena.summary: Dry austral winter–spring period (Jun/Jul–Oct) across the central and southern Amazon. Falling rainfall dries surface soils and stresses canopy moisture, prepping both natural floodplains and human agricultural frontiers for late-dry extremes.

sar_physics.roughness_mechanism: Standing terra firme tree geometry remains physically rough, so spatial texture persists even as radar brightness shifts with moisture; dried pasture grasses look smoother.
sar_physics.dielectric_mechanism: Reduced leaf water potential and lower topsoil moisture decrease the surface dielectric constant across sunlit uplands, lowering C-band VH cross-polarization by -0.8 to -1.8 dB.
sar_physics.polarization_note: VH / VV ratio isolates canopy water content changes separately from soil roughness variations.
sar_physics.frequency_comparison: C-band (5.6 cm) senses rapid top-leaf water stress during dry spells, while L-band (24 cm) remains stable over deep woody trunks unless drought causes branch dieback.

drivers.natural_driver: Seasonal northward ITCZ shift (Jun–Oct), amplified strongly during El Niño & warm Tropical North Atlantic phases.
drivers.human_driver: Dry-season soil firming enables heavy machinery access along frontier roads (BR-230, BR-319).

phenomena.name: Clearing / land opening
phenomena.summary: Human-driven forest felling and fishbone pasture expansion concentrated during the dry Jun–Oct ground-access window along Southern Amazonas corridors (Apuí–Lábrea / BR-230).

sar_physics.primary_sensitivity: Volume Roughness Loss (3D Forest -> Smooth Bare Soil)
sar_physics.roughness_mechanism: Intact rainforest is a deep 3D volume of randomly oriented branches and leaves (strong depolarizing volume scatter). Felling replaces this with flat cleared soil/pasture, collapsing volume scattering in sharp rectangular geometric plots.
sar_physics.dielectric_mechanism: Freshly felled logs briefly retain sap water, then dry rapidly under sun—making clearings persistently darker in cross-polarization regardless of afternoon cloud cover.
sar_physics.polarization_note: Cross-polarization (Sentinel-1 VH and NISAR HV) is the premier deforestation detector: VH drops -2 to -6 dB immediately after felling.
sar_physics.frequency_comparison: C-band (5.6 cm) detects early understory/crown thinning; L-band (24 cm) directly measures loss of heavy woody trunks and aboveground carbon biomass (~150+ Mg/ha drop).

drivers.natural_driver: Drier Jun–Oct terrain permits bulldozers and chainsaws to enter upland terra firme.
drivers.human_driver: Cattle pasture conversion, speculative land grabbing along BR-230 Trans-Amazonian & BR-319 roads.

legend.label: Green: L-band HVHV Woody Canopy Biomass

phenomena.name: Fire season
phenomena.summary: Peak Amazon burning season (Aug–Oct, climaxing in Sep). Thick smoke chokes optical imaging for weeks—precisely where active SAR microwave pulses see through smoke plumes to map burned scars alongside NASA FIRMS thermal detections.

sar_physics.primary_sensitivity: Roughness Shift + Smoke-Penetrating Burn Scar Mapping
sar_physics.roughness_mechanism: Fire consumes fine leaves and twigs (reducing cross-pol volume scatter) while leaving charred bare soil and skeletal standing snags exposed to radar pulses.
sar_physics.dielectric_mechanism: Intense heat vaporizes surface soil and litter moisture, dropping the surface dielectric constant sharply until the first Nov–Dec rains trigger post-fire ash runoff.
sar_physics.polarization_note: Pre-fire vs. post-fire ΔVH (-2.0 to -4.5 dB drop) combined with NASA FIRMS thermal hotspots separates active burn scars from unburned smoke-covered forest.
sar_physics.frequency_comparison: Both C-band (5.6 cm) and L-band (24 cm) penetrate dense biomass smoke without attenuation; L-band distinguishes understory ground fires (snags left) from stand-replacing clear-cuts.

drivers.natural_driver: Late-dry VPD spike and drought-desiccated litter turn escaped agricultural fires into megafires.
drivers.human_driver: Broadcast ignition of Jun–Aug felled slash to clear pastures and enrich soil ash nutrients.

phenomena.name: Low river levels
phenomena.summary: Annual Amazon hydrologic trough (Aug–Oct, lowest stage ~Sep/Oct). Shrinking channels expose kilometer-wide sandbars, mudflats, and bedrock rapids—severing river transport for rural communities across the Madeira, Solimões, and Rio Negro.

sar_physics.primary_sensitivity: Roughness Inversion (Smooth Mirror Water -> Bright Rough Sandbars)
sar_physics.roughness_mechanism: When flooded, smooth river water reflects microwaves away like a mirror (<-16 dB). As water drops in Sep–Oct, rippled sandbars, mudflats, and rocks replace water—jumping +4 to +8 dB brighter in C- and L-band!
sar_physics.dielectric_mechanism: Drying exposed riverbeds rapidly lose water dielectric response while gaining rough geometric micro-relief that backscatters strongly to SAR.
sar_physics.polarization_note: OPERA DSWx-S1 shrinks water masks cleanly to thin low-flow threads while ΔVV highlights every newly exposed sandbar shoal blocking river barges.
sar_physics.frequency_comparison: C-band (5.6 cm) is acutely sensitive to small centimeter-scale sand ripples on newly exposed bars; L-band (24 cm) differentiates smoother wet mudflats from coarser cobbles.

drivers.natural_driver: Seasonal baseflow recession peaking Sep–Oct, pushed to extremes by 2023/2024 warm-Atlantic/El Niño droughts.
drivers.human_driver: Marooned river supply barges, drinking-water shortages, and hydropower generation cuts on Rio Madeira.

events.name: Australia Black Summer Burn Scars
events.summary: Sentinel-1 C-band cross-polarized VH backscatter penetrates pyrocumulonimbus smoke clouds over Clyde Mountain & Batemans Bay (NSW), revealing structural branch/canopy incineration immediately after Jan 2020.

sar_physics.primary_sensitivity: Crown Volume Roughness + Ash Soil Moisture
sar_physics.roughness_mechanism: Charred eucalypt crowns lose small leaves/twigs responsible for C-band VH volume scattering, causing a sharp ΔVH drop.
sar_physics.dielectric_mechanism: Pyrolysis desiccates surface fuel (low εr) until ash exposes bare soil dielectric contrast.
sar_physics.polarization_note: VH/VV ratio drops immediately across high-intensity crown fire corridors.
sar_physics.frequency_comparison: C-band (5.6 cm) maps leaf/twig scorch within days; L-band (24 cm) persists years to track trunk mortality.

drivers.natural_driver: Record positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) & prolonged 2019 extreme heatwave/lightning ignitions.
drivers.human_driver: Anthropogenic climate warming lengthened NSW fire-weather index beyond historical baselines.

comparison_pair.delta_summary: 8.1% severe crown loss + 8.0% moderate understory scorch

events.name: Record Rio Negro flood (Manaus)
events.headline_metric: 30.02 m crest at Porto de Manaus (119-yr record, Jun 2021)
events.summary: In June 2021, the Rio Negro crested at an all-time record 30.02 m in Manaus after intense La Niña rainfall. Sentinel-1 C-band and ALOS-2 L-band SAR expose both expanded open channels and miles of submerged igapó/várzea forest hidden beneath intact tree crowns.

sar_physics.roughness_mechanism: Calm flood lakes act as smooth specular mirrors (VV < -15 dB, dark cyan), while flooded tree trunks create intense vertical-horizontal corner reflectors (emerald/violet).
sar_physics.dielectric_mechanism: Rising water fills the floodplain floor with εr ≈ 80 liquid water, jumping trunk–water dihedral backscatter +3.8 to +5.5 dB higher than the Oct 2020 low-water baseline.
sar_physics.polarization_note: Compare Event Peak (Jun 2021) vs. Low-Water Baseline (Oct 2020): VV double-bounce + HH L-band penetration reveal where water stood inside closed forest.
sar_physics.frequency_comparison: C-band (5.6 cm) captures open flooded avenues and low várzea scrub; 24 cm L-band penetrates tall dense igapó crowns along Rio Negro islands.

drivers.natural_driver: La Niña convective reinforcement flooded the northern Negro & western Solimões sub-basins simultaneously.
drivers.human_driver: Submerged urban waterfronts, floating bridges, and inundated peri-urban neighborhoods in Manaus & Iranduba.

events.name: Pakistan Indus Inland Sea Flood
events.headline_metric: +14.0% newly inundated Indus basin cropland & towns (VV ≤ -15 dB)
events.summary: Extreme 2022 monsoon created a ~100 km wide inland sea around Lake Manchar & Dadu in Sindh. Smooth mirror-like floodwaters reflect C-band radar away from Sentinel-1, turning inundated plains jet-black (< -15 dB).

sar_physics.roughness_mechanism: Flooded agricultural fields replace rough diffuse soil/crops with wind-sheltered flat water mirrors.
sar_physics.dielectric_mechanism: Liquid water's high dielectric constant produces near-total forward specular reflection away from the SAR antenna.
sar_physics.polarization_note: VV co-polarization shows maximum water-vs-dry-land drop (-18 dB water vs -9 dB farmland).
sar_physics.frequency_comparison: Both C-band and NISAR L-band penetrate relentless Aug 2022 monsoon cloud decks that hid the peak flood from optical sensors.

drivers.natural_driver: 2022 La Niña atmospheric river & record monsoon stalling over Sindh + accelerated glacial melt.
drivers.human_driver: Embankment breaches along Right Bank Outfall Drain (RBOD) and floodplain settlement density.

comparison_pair.delta_summary: +14.0% newly submerged alluvial plain detected through monsoon clouds

events.name: Türkiye–Syria Fault Slip & Urban Damage
events.headline_metric: 4.2 m left-lateral fault rupture & 28.44% urban |ΔVV| ≥ 2.2 dB change
events.summary: Synthetic Aperture Radar measures centimeter-to-meter crustal deformation across the East Anatolian Fault near Pazarcik and maps structural urban collapse via Sentinel-1 corner-reflector phase & amplitude decorrelation.

sar_physics.primary_sensitivity: Interferometric Phase (Range Slip) + Urban Corner-Reflector Geometry
sar_physics.roughness_mechanism: Intact city blocks act as coherent dihedral wall–ground reflectors; building collapse scrambles phase coherence and shifts |ΔVV|.
sar_physics.dielectric_mechanism: Mid-winter dry stone rubble keeps dielectric variance low while geometric range shifts encode fault displacement.
sar_physics.polarization_note: VV amplitude + InSAR interferometric phase pairs resolve both vertical uplift and strike-slip shear across the fault.
sar_physics.frequency_comparison: C-band (5.6 cm) saturates very near high-gradient fault cores, where NISAR L-band (24 cm) preserves fringe coherence.

drivers.natural_driver: Mw 7.8 strike-slip rupture along the East Anatolian Fault Zone (2023-02-06) + Mw 7.5 Elbistan trigger.
drivers.human_driver: Multi-story unreinforced masonry & soft-story urban construction concentrated across fault basins.

comparison_pair.delta_summary: 4.2 m coseismic fault offset & 28.44% Sentinel-1 intensity disruption

events.name: Canada Boreal Permafrost & Taiga Megafires
events.summary: During Canada's historic 2023 wildfire season (>15M ha burned nationally), continental smoke cloaked North America for weeks while Sentinel-1 C-band VH radar continuously mapped expanding James Bay & Quebec burn scars.

sar_physics.primary_sensitivity: Boreal Canopy Loss + Peat/Permafrost Thaw Moisture
sar_physics.roughness_mechanism: Loss of dense black spruce branches eliminates C-band cross-pol VH volume scattering.
sar_physics.dielectric_mechanism: Removed insulating moss mat accelerates active-layer permafrost thaw, altering exposed bog soil moisture.
sar_physics.polarization_note: Negative ΔVH highlights tree death while post-fire HH/VV tracks wet charred peatland pockets.
sar_physics.frequency_comparison: C-band tracks fine needle burn scars rapidly; NISAR L-band monitors multi-year subsidence as permafrost thaws.

drivers.natural_driver: Early May snowmelt, spring lightning clusters, and persistent high-pressure Omega ridges over Quebec.
drivers.human_driver: Arctic amplification warming (>2x global average) dried deep boreal organic peat layers.

comparison_pair.delta_summary: 3.67% severe crown loss beneath transcontinental smoke plumes

events.name: Antarctic Winter Sea-Ice Record Deficit
events.headline_metric: -15.15% missing Haakon VII / Weddell winter pack ice vs 2020-09 (6σ climate anomaly)
events.summary: In September 2023—supposed to be peak Austral winter freeze—Antarctic sea ice fell >1.6 million km² below its 1981–2010 maximum. Active SAR and passive microwave AMSR2 pierce polar night and Southern Ocean storms.

sar_physics.primary_sensitivity: Brine-Salt Dielectric Change + Floe Ridge Roughness
sar_physics.roughness_mechanism: Ridged deformed pack ice produces bright microwave scattering compared to dark wind-sheltered pancake/frazil leads.
sar_physics.dielectric_mechanism: Seawater salt expulsion lowers first-year sea ice permittivity (εr ~3.5 vs ~80 open polar ocean).
sar_physics.polarization_note: HH/HV SAR + AMSR2 brightness temperature cleanly separate drifting icebergs, thin leads, and perennial fast ice.
sar_physics.frequency_comparison: NISAR L-band (24 cm) penetrates surface snow metamorphism to map sea-ice motion & calving continuously at polar night.

drivers.natural_driver: Warm subsurface Southern Ocean circumpolar upwelling & poleward storm heat transport.
drivers.human_driver: Long-term ocean heat uptake destabilized the winter refreeze feedback after 2016.

comparison_pair.delta_summary: 15.15% of the Haakon VII / Weddell marginal ice belt remained unfrozen open ocean at winter max

events.name: Severe drought
events.headline_metric: Manaus 12.70 m · Lake Tefé 39.1 °C & dramatic shoreline contraction
events.summary: From September to November 2023, an extraordinary El Niño + warm Tropical North Atlantic drought shrank central Amazon lakes and rivers. Over Lake Tefé & Rio Solimões, Sentinel-1 SAR maps wide dark open water turning into bright radar-rough exposed mudflats and sandbars.

sar_physics.primary_sensitivity: Roughness Inversion as Specular Lake Becomes Exposed Mudflats
sar_physics.roughness_mechanism: Receding Lake Tefé shoreline replaces mirror-smooth open water (-17 dB) with rough cracked silt beds and sandbars (-9 to -5 dB), producing a dramatic +6 dB brightening.
sar_physics.dielectric_mechanism: Loss of open surface water and drying várzea soil drops dielectric wetness across hundreds of square kilometers of formerly submerged Mamirauá wetlands.
sar_physics.polarization_note: Sentinel-1 VV cleanly delineates the shrinking water polygon (-Water contraction mask) between May 2023 High Water and Oct 2023 Extreme Drought.
sar_physics.frequency_comparison: C-band (5.6 cm) VV sharply resolves every newly stranded sandbank along Solimões meanders and Lake Tefé thermal refuges.

drivers.natural_driver: Compound 2023 El Niño + record North Atlantic sea-surface heat suppressed wet-season inflow and triggered Oct extremes.
drivers.human_driver: Isolated river towns requiring emergency barges; mass dolphin mortality in shallowed 39.1 °C Lake Tefé.

comparison_pair.delta_summary: -13.45% water area contracted into rough sandbars/mudflats

events.name: Record drought and fires
events.headline_metric: Manaus record 12.11 m · 140,328 INPE biome fire hotspots (Aug–Oct 2024)
events.summary: Worse than 2023: Aug–Oct 2024 broke all-time low water records (Manaus 12.11 m, Madeira 1.24 m) while fueling massive fires across southern Amazonas (Apuí–Lábrea). Cloud- & smoke-penetrating Sentinel-1 ΔVH exposes deforestation clearings and fire scars hidden beneath choking smoke.

sar_physics.primary_sensitivity: Volume Scattering Loss & Smoke-Penetrating Burn Scars
sar_physics.roughness_mechanism: Freshly burned and cleared plots lose dense foliage volume scatterers, causing C-band VH backscatter to plummet -2.0 to -4.8 dB along BR-230 expansion fishbones.
sar_physics.dielectric_mechanism: Extreme dry-season VPD dries dead slash and standing peat/litter soils, allowing fires to spread into untouched upland forest edges.
sar_physics.polarization_note: Pre-fire (Jul 2024) vs. Post-fire (Oct 2024) Sentinel-1 VH difference directly maps structural canopy loss beneath thick optical smoke haze.
sar_physics.frequency_comparison: Fusing NASA FIRMS thermal detections (8–10 μm infrared) with 5.6 cm SAR VH change locates both active flame fronts and lasting structural canopy scars.

drivers.natural_driver: Multi-year 2023–2024 precipitation deficit left Amazon soils parched ahead of Aug–Oct 2024 heat.
drivers.human_driver: Intentional Jun–Aug clearing along BR-230 escaped into drought-stressed rainforest during Sep ignition.

comparison_pair.delta_summary: 4.22% canopy ΔVH ≤ -2 dB (0.13% severe) · 5,144 high-conf fires

events.name: NISAR L-band acquisitions
events.headline_metric: NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band (24 cm) GCOV Validated Passes (Oct–Nov 2026 vs Jun 2026)
events.summary: Real validated NASA-ISRO NISAR Level-2 GCOV dual-polarization (HHHH + HVHV) acquisitions over Manaus & the Amazon Basin (Oct 21 & Nov 2, 2026, Track 140), compared directly with June 2026 flood-peak NISAR data and simultaneous NASA OPERA Sentinel-1 C-band masks.

sar_physics.primary_sensitivity: 24 cm L-Band Sub-Canopy Penetration & Co/Cross-Pol Separation
sar_physics.roughness_mechanism: NISAR's 24 cm L-band wavelength passes through small twigs/leaves to scatter off major trunks, soil surface roughness, and smooth blackwater Rio Negro channels.
sar_physics.dielectric_mechanism: Comparing Jun 2026 flood peak vs. Oct–Nov 2026 dry transition on identical Track 140 shows flooded-forest HHHH double-bounce turning back to dry forest floor scattering.
sar_physics.polarization_note: HHHH (co-pol) highlights specular water darkness and trunk-water double-bounce brightness; HVHV (cross-pol) quantitatively measures 3D woody forest biomass density.
sar_physics.frequency_comparison: Overlay NISAR L-band (24 cm) beside simultaneous NASA OPERA DSWx-S1 Sentinel-1 C-band (5.6 cm) from Oct 2026 to see deep sub-canopy structure vs. upper-crown sensitivity.

drivers.natural_driver: 2026 Rio Negro flood-to-dry seasonal pulse captured across identical 12-day repeat NISAR orbits.
drivers.human_driver: First operational L-band radar baseline over Manaus wetlands & Amazon deforestation arcs (Apuí & Madeira).

comparison_pair.delta_summary: L-band HHHH median -6.6 dB vs HVHV -11.61 dB (+5.01 dB co/cross pol gap)
